sources.title: Codex repository contributor instructions
sources.supports: Declared architectural ownership, bounded structured context as a contributor requirement, and documentation policy.
sources.limitations: States intended maintainer rules; it does not prove every runtime path enforces them.

sources.title: Core session engine
sources.supports: Live session ownership, operation/event flow, approval waiters, cancellation, and persistence integration.
sources.limitations: A large module; claims about an individual task or tool require its concrete implementation too.

sources.title: Turn sampling loop
sources.supports: Per-turn settings/context construction, streaming model sampling, tool execution, and repeated sampling.
sources.limitations: Provider adapters and specialized tasks can add behavior outside this file.

sources.title: Tool router, registry, orchestrator, and specification plan
sources.supports: Call parsing, registry dispatch, hooks/lifecycle wrapping, result conversion, model-visible specification selection, and controlled parallel execution.
sources.limitations: Generic dispatch does not itself establish every handler's authorization boundary; registered and model-visible tools are distinct sets.

sources.title: Tool router and specification-plan tests
sources.supports: Concrete examples of typed routing and conditional tool exposure at the pinned commit.
sources.limitations: Tests cover selected cases and are not a proof of universal behavior.

sources.title: Execution approval policy and sandbox selection
sources.supports: Three-way execution decisions and separate local shell/patch sandbox construction.
sources.limitations: Does not govern every remote MCP, connector, search, or service-side authorization decision.

sources.title: Context history, normalization, compaction, and truncation
sources.supports: Model context is a derived projection; incomplete tool-call pairs are normalized; compaction/truncation handle context pressure.
sources.limitations: The normalizer establishes a usable pairing rule but does not by itself prove global uniqueness of outputs; limits can still produce visible failure.

sources.title: Context history and normalization tests
sources.supports: Observed normalization behavior for interrupted and malformed transcript shapes.
sources.limitations: Only the encoded cases are established.

sources.title: Thread lifecycle, store, and rollout reconstruction
sources.supports: Stable thread identity, recorded history, reconstruction into a new live session, and fork behavior.
sources.limitations: Persistence availability varies for ephemeral sessions and store configuration.

sources.title: Rollout recorder and compression
sources.supports: Append-oriented rollout recording, recovery from interrupted tails, flushing, and derived compacted records.
sources.limitations: The record is not literally immutable or necessarily a complete audit of every external side effect.

sources.title: Rollout recorder tests
sources.supports: Selected recorder recovery and persistence behavior at the pinned commit.
sources.limitations: Does not establish storage durability under every OS/filesystem failure mode.

sources.title: Codex app-server protocol guide
sources.supports: Declared JSON-RPC lifecycle, connection handshake, bounded queues, thread/turn/item APIs, bidirectional requests, experimental opt-in, and schema workflow.
sources.limitations: Large evolving reference; code and protocol types remain authoritative for exact field behavior.

sources.title: App-server connection and message processing
sources.supports: Implementation backing for the app-server's high-level connection and lifecycle contracts.
sources.limitations: Does not by itself cover every processor named in the reference catalog.

sources.title: App-server connection and v2 integration tests
sources.supports: End-to-end examples for major v2 lifecycle and connection contracts.
sources.limitations: Test coverage is broad but not exhaustive of the API catalog.

sources.title: App-server protocol definitions
sources.supports: Authoritative checked-in method names, wire types, and versioned protocol structure at the pinned commit.
sources.limitations: Type declarations do not prove that every declared behavior succeeds at runtime.

sources.title: Core protocol v1 overview
sources.supports: Historical terminology, SQ/EQ conceptual interface, compatibility serialization, and its own explicit warning that code may differ.
sources.limitations: Not a current authoritative specification; several lifecycle descriptions reflect older architecture.

sources.title: Codex MCP server interface
sources.supports: Declared experimental MCP control interface and its mapping to v2 app-server-style methods/events.
sources.limitations: Explicitly unstable and subordinate to protocol types plus server wiring.

sources.title: codex-core runtime support matrix
sources.supports: Declared platform-specific sandbox helpers, policy routing, compatibility, and fail-closed cases.
sources.limitations: A support contract, not a substitute for platform implementation and integration tests.

sources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare Mathematics for Computer Science: predicates and sets
inspected_locations: lecture note landing page and predicates/sets description
sources.supports: Optional background for the elementary set and predicate notation used by the formal page.
sources.limitations: Does not support any Codex implementation claim.

sources.title: Leslie Lamport's State Machines in TLA+ and TLA+ video course
sources.supports: Optional primary-author background for state/transition and temporal-specification concepts.
sources.limitations: Does not make the guide a TLA+ specification or prove its properties.
